{{Quote|Flew all my life. Flew everywhere I could manage, and you know what? I couldn't get to a hundredth of what's out there. Couldn't get to a millionth. But it was fun trying. A whole lot of fun.|The pilot|<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] '''pilot''' served in the [[Republic Starfighter Corps/Legends|Republic Starfighter Corps]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the conflict known as the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], flying to many [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] before retiring in [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]] due to old age and eventually settling on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] saw the young [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] [[Youngling/Legends|boy]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] participate in a [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]]. After the race, the pilot met Skywalker and his friends at [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa's]] [[Mos Espa marketplace|marketplace]], where he shared with them stories of his past exploits and encouraged Skywalker to pursue his dream of becoming a [[Realspace/Legends|space]] pilot. The old pilot would continue to spend [[Time/Legends|time]] with Skywalker on occasion and entertain him with more stories. Among many things, the pilot told Skywalker about the mysterious [[Diathim/Legends|Angels]] of the planet [[Iego/Legends|Iego]] and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].

==Biography==
{{Dialogue|The pilot|Flew a cruiser filled with Republic soldiers into Makem Te during its rebellion. That was a scary business. Flew Jedi Knights once upon a time, too.|Banai|Jedi! Wow!|Skywalker|Really? You really flew Jedi?|The pilot|Cross my heart and call me bantha fodder if I'm lying. It was a long time ago, but I flew four of them to a place I'm not supposed to talk about even now. Told you. I've been everywhere a man can get to in one lifetime. Everywhere.|attr=The pilot tells about his exploits to Anakin Skywalker and Kitster Banai|src=<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] served in the [[Republic Starfighter Corps/Legends|Republic Starfighter Corps]] during the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. During his career in the [[Corps/Legends|corps]], the pilot flew a [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] with Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Makem Te/Legends|Makem Te]] during the Republic's efforts to stop the [[Makem Te rebellion|rebellion]]<ref name="TPM novel" /> instigated by the local cult known as the [[Temple of the Beatific Razor]].<ref name="Geonosis">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> On another occasion, he flew a team of four [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] on a mission and was forbidden to talk about the place he had taken them. The pilot also successfully flew through the notorious [[Kessel Run/Legends|Kessel Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace route]], although many of his peers had tried to discourage him from doing so due to the dangerous nature of the route.<ref name="TPM novel" /> In [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]],<ref name="TPM novel date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], which establishes the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] retired six [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior.</ref> having visited a large number of worlds and believing himself to be too old for his profession, the pilot retired from the corps.<ref name="TPM novel" />

Around [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]],<ref name="Journal date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]'' to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], which establishes the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] landed on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] prior.</ref> the pilot landed on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] with no fuel or money. Content with spending the rest of his [[Standard day/Legends|days]] in the shade of the planet's [[Binary star/Legends|twin stars]], he gladly shared stories of his past travels with anyone who wanted to listen.<ref name="Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref> On one occasion, while in the [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]], he went to the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]] to see a [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]] that took place there. The pilot took notice of one of the [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racers]], the [[Youngling/Legends|young boy]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who demonstrated great skill with the [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|vehicle]], although he crashed his [[Podracer/Legends|pod]] at the end of the race. Later that day, the pilot visited the [[Mos Espa marketplace]], where he noticed Skywalker discussing [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] with his friends [[Kitster Chanchani Banai|Kitster Banai]] and [[W. Wald]]. Intervening in their discussion, the pilot bought himself and the boys some [[ruby bliel]]s&mdash;a beverage popular on Tatooine&mdash;and went on to tell them about his exploits, much to the youngsters' amazement. Skywalker confessed to him that he wanted to become a pilot himself, but Wald believed that the Human boy would not succeed since he was a [[Slavery/Legends|slave]]. Telling Skywalker about his experience with the Kessel Run, the old pilot encouraged the boy to pursue his dream no matter what.<ref name="TPM novel" />

[[File:Pilot_and_Skywalker.jpg|thumb|left|230px|The pilot talking to Skywalker at Maggy the Gorgon's]]
In Mos Espa, the pilot frequented [[Maggy the Gorgon's]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], where he met Skywalker and his friends and entertained them with more stories from his past.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II||Maggy the Gorgon's}}</ref> The pilot told Skywalker more stories about the Jedi, informing him that the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] generally only accepted very young children&mdash;who did not yet reach one year old&mdash;for [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]]. He also told Skywalker about the so-called "[[Diathim/Legends|Angels]]" from the planet [[Iego/Legends|Iego]], who were rumored to be the most beautiful creatures in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. On another occasion, the pilot was sitting outside the cantina at the Mos Espa marketplace when he saw the boy passing by and waved to him, inviting a conversation. However, the pilot was shocked when the boy asked him if he knew anything about the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]; the man was frightened at the very thought of the return of the ancient [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] cult. It turned out that Skywalker had merely found the remains of an old [[Battle droid/Legends|war droid]] and saw an old [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] recording that mentioned the Sith Order. Relieved, the old pilot told the boy that [[New Sith|the Sith Order]] was [[Fourth Great Schism|founded]] by a [[Darth Ruin/Legends|rogue Jedi Knight]] [[2000 BBY/Legends|thousands of years ago]]. [[1000 BBY/Legends|A millennium later]], the Sith were believed to have been [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|destroyed]], although rumors remained that [[Darth Bane/Legends|one Sith Lord]] survived to pass on their teachings.<ref name="Journal" /> In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="Anakin date">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Episode I: Anakin Skywalker]]'' to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> shortly before the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] podrace, the pilot visited Maggy the Gorgon's, where he shared a drink with a [[Unidentified Duros assassin|Duros assassin]]. Soon, a fistfight broke out between the Boonta pilots who spent their [[Time/Legends|time]] there. As the situation heated, the pilot took a ruby bliel and exited the cantina, following one of the other patrons that was thrown out during the fight.<ref name="Anakin Skywalker" />

Outside, the pilot witnessed a standoff between Skywalker and the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] podracer pilot [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], with Banai and Wald also present. Taking an imposing posture, he inquired as to what was going on. Assuring the pilot that he meant no harm to the boy, Sebulba quickly left the scene. Advising the boys not to go into Maggy the Gorgon's, the pilot gave them his ruby bliel, and Banai and Wald left. Before Skywalker joined his friends, he asked the pilot to tell him about the Angels again the next time he visited the cantina. The pilot agreed and returned to his [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] companion inside the cantina. When the Duros asked him why he bothered talking with a slave, the pilot replied that he sensed something special about the boy. Hearing those words, the Duros jokingly stated that the pilot sounded like a Jedi, but the latter laughed it off.<ref name="Anakin Skywalker" /><ref name="TPM 1/2">[[Episode I: The Phantom Menace ½|''Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' ½]]</ref> Not long after that, Skywalker indeed found himself behind the controls of a [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], helping to put an end to the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="TPM novel" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Well, in this life you're often born one thing and die another. You don't have to accept that what you're given when you come in is all you'll have when you leave.|The pilot, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
The gruff<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|56|Unseen Planets of Episode I}}</ref> old [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] was a tall, lean, and corded man, with a weatherworn and [[Star/Legends|sun]]-browned face and [[Hair/Legends|hair]] cut short.<ref name="TPM novel" /> He had distinctly styled gray-colored facial hair, which consisted of a full beard, shaved at the chin with the exception of a small strap of hair there.<ref name="Anakin Skywalker" /> The man possessed [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that were an odd [[Color/Legends|color]] of gray, and a warm and ironic smile. Despite having traveled a lot around the galaxy during his days at the corps, he still believed that he was far from seeing all the wonders of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. When he realized that he had become too old for his profession, he retired<ref name="TPM novel" /> and enjoyed telling tall tales to gullible audiences.<ref name="Insider" /> The pilot was a determined man, following through with his idea to fly the Kessel Run despite all the discouragement he had received. When he saw Anakin Skywalker handling a pod, the spacer was very impressed by the boy's skill, believing that Skywalker was better at flying than he himself had been at twice the boy's age. When Skywalker expressed his desire to become a space pilot, the old man supported him, telling the boy that he should not accept his fate as a slave as permanent.<ref name="TPM novel" />

The pilot's experience told him that Skywalker would succeed in his dream; the feeling was so strong that his Duros companion compared it to a Jedi's [[Force sense/Legends|Force sense]].<ref name="TPM 1/2" /> In terms of starfighters, the pilot had a preference for the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]].<ref name="TPM novel" /> The pilot was afraid of the return of the Sith, and became visibly frightened when Skywalker mentioned that ancient order.<ref name="Journal" /> However, he could also be rather frightening himself, forcing Sebulba to quickly retreat during the standoff at Maggy the Gorgon's.<ref name="Anakin Skywalker" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You have to trust your dreams. Or they'll never come true. But dreams are funny. Even when they come true, it's never how you ''think'' they will. There are always a few surprises along the way.|The pilot, to Anakin Skywalker in ''Anakin's Fate''|<ref name="Anakin's Fate">''[[Anakin's Fate]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Republic_pilot.jpg|thumb|right|100px|The pilot as depicted in ''Anakin's Fate'']]
The retired pilot first appeared in [[Terry Brooks]]' [[1999]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM novel" /> The scene where Anakin Skywalker meets a space pilot after his unfortunate race is also featured in ''[[Anakin's Fate]]'', a storybook written by [[Marc Cerasini]] and illustrated by [[John Alvin]]. However, ''Anakin's Fate'' contradicts ''The Phantom Menace'' novel in a number of ways. In the storybook, instead of Wald, Skywalker is accompanied by a boy named [[Seek/Legends|Seek]]. Instead of the old veteran depicted in the novel, the space pilot is portrayed as a young man. The dialogue between him and Skywalker is also different. Instead of talking about his past career, the young pilot only tells Skywalker to pursue his dreams, believing that the boy flies better than he himself did at his age.<ref name="Anakin's Fate" /> [[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker|''Star Wars Episode I Journal: Anakin Skywalker'']] featured the pilot, establishing that he was the one who told Skywalker about the Angels of Iego.<ref name="Journal" /> The comic book [[Episode I: The Phantom Menace ½|''Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' ½]] featured a space pilot visiting Maggy the Gorgon's, and also had Skywalker asking that pilot to tell him about the Angels again, thus establishing that the pilot is the same character as the one from ''The Phantom Menace'' novel and the ''Episode I Journal.''<ref name="Anakin Skywalker" /><ref name="TPM 1/2" />
